question: to the Commission Ewa Zajączkowska-Hernik (PfE) Subject:

According to a recent article published by ‘Politico’, air conditioning on floors 1 to 7 of the Commission’s headquarters in the Berlaymont building, which are used by staff, was switched off due to the heat wave. But the air conditioning on the upper floors where the offices of the Commissioners are located continued to operate. This blatant double standard sparked outrage among both the public and the staff, who described the situation as ‘feudalism’. In light of this: 1.
How does the Commission justify this internal double standard, where senior European officials continue to use air-conditioned offices while lower-level workers are forced to work in extreme heat?

Does the Commission consider that the breakdown of the cooling infrastructure in the Berlaymont building and the power cuts in the European Parliament prove that the current EU climate and energy policy leads to unstable infrastructure that is unable to meet basic technical requirements?
Given this situation, is the Commission planning to revise its green transition directives since the imposed standards on working conditions cannot be met even in its own headquarters?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.9.2026) 1. Due to technical reasons, the air conditioning system in the Berlaymont building had to be progressively switched off on Friday 26 June 2026, in the afternoon, floor by floor. Before the end of the day, the entire building was without a cooling system. This was done to prevent the cooling system from stalling, which could have led to more long-lasting consequences. 2. The Commission has not experienced a breakdown of the cooling infrastructure in the Berlaymont building. The incident in question was an isolated case. The Commission is not in a position to comment on the alleged power cuts in the European Parliament. 3. The working conditions in the buildings, including the indoor temperature, are governed by national laws. The Commission is committed to ensuring proper working conditions for its staff.
